![claude-bughunter banner](assets/banner-v2.svg) # claude-bughunter > A self-contained Claude skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work · **84 skills** · 15 slash commands · **681 disclosed-report patterns** (433 now individually cited & auditable) across 24 core vulnerability classes · enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices · engagement-folder scaffolding · Burp MCP integration · battle-tested across authorized red-team and bug-hunting engagements, plus public training platforms (DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop, Hacker101, testphp.vulnweb.com). Built by **[Sachin Sharma](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sachinsharma8080/)** — Bug Hunting & GenAI Security Research.

SPONSORED BY

      

--- ## What is this? `claude-bughunter` is a drop-in skill bundle for the [Claude Code skills system](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills). Install once and Claude Code stops being a chatbot and starts behaving like a senior bug-hunting researcher or red-team operator: it knows the techniques, the chain templates, the VRT mappings, the platform CVE chains, and the hygiene — and it stays in scope. Four layers stack: - **Think** — `bb-methodology` + `redteam-mindset`: the 5-phase non-linear workflow, critical-thinking framework, and red-team operator discipline. - **Hunt webapps** — 58 `hunt-*` skills curated from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports: per-class detection patterns, payloads, bypass tables, and chain templates. - **Hit the perimeter** — enterprise platform chains (M365/Entra, Okta, vCenter, SSL-VPN appliances, SharePoint, cloud IAM): current 2024–2026 CVE chains + post-credential escalation. - **Ship it** — `triage-validation` + reporting + `evidence-hygiene`: the 7-Question Gate, VRT-aware severity, OOS rebuttals, PII redaction, and red-team deliverables. All triggered automatically by topic — describe what you're testing in plain English and the relevant skill loads. No invocation by name. --- ## Quickstart **Option A — install as a Claude Code plugin (recommended).** From inside Claude Code: ```text /plugin marketplace add elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter /plugin install claude-bughunter@elementalsouls ``` All 84 skills + 15 commands load namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` and update when you bump the plugin version — no files copied into `~/.claude/`. **A HackerOne account is optional.** The install asks for a HackerOne API username and token. They only let the HackerOne MCP read your private programs and your own reports; leave both blank if you don't need that. Every skill, command and the MCP's public tools (duplicate search, program scope) work without them. **Option B — copy install (no plugin system / pin to a clone):** ```bash git clone https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter.git cd Claude-BugHunter ``` ```bash # macOS / Linux bash scripts/install.sh # Windows (PowerShell) pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1 ``` Both copy the skills + commands into `~/.claude/` (macOS/Linux) or `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (Windows) and wire the `hunt` engagement scaffolder. **What each install path gives you:** | Path | 84 skills + 15 slash commands | `cbh` CLI | `hunt` scaffolder | |---|---|---|---| | **A — plugin** | ✅ namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` | ➕ separate `pipx install` | ❌ clone-only | | **B — copy install** | ✅ copied into `~/.claude/` | ✅ from the clone | ✅ from the clone | The plugin is the fastest path to the skills + slash commands. The terminal-native `cbh` runner installs standalone — `pipx install git+https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter` — so plugin users can add it without a full clone (see [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md)). The `hunt` engagement scaffolder ships with the clone (Option B). That's it. Open Claude Code and describe what you're testing in plain English — the right skill loads automatically, no invocation by name: ```text > Testing acme.com — an in-scope HackerOne target. Run recon and rank the surface. ⟳ loading skills: web2-recon, offensive-osint, bb-methodology … → subdomain enum (subfinder + crt.sh) … 47 hosts → live hosts (httpx) … 12 · tech fingerprint … 6 distinct stacks → ranked surface: api.acme.com (GraphQL, introspection ON) ← start here auth.acme.com (OAuth, SSO) ← hunt-oauth Next: want me to probe the GraphQL introspection + OAuth redirect_uri? ``` → Full [Installation guide](INSTALL.md) · [Usage guide](USAGE.md) · [searchable skill catalog](docs/skills.md). > The block above is an illustrative transcript. To record a real demo of your own session: `asciinema rec demo.cast` → upload to [asciinema.org](https://asciinema.org) and drop the badge here. --- ## Runs on multiple agent harnesses ![One install, agent harnesses — Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Hermes Agent, Google AntiGravity](assets/harness-routing.svg) The skills are plain [Agent Skills](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills) — the same `SKILL.md` format that **Claude Code · OpenCode · OpenAI Codex CLI · Hermes Agent · Google AntiGravity** all load. One command installs them everywhere: ```bash # macOS / Linux bash scripts/install.sh --all --burp-mcp # Windows (PowerShell) pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1 -All -BurpMcp ``` | Harness | Target Skill Directory | Flag | |---|---|---| | **Claude Code** (baseline) | `~/.claude/skills/` | *(default)* | | **OpenCode** | reads `~/.claude/skills/` & `~/.agents/skills/` | *(default)* / `--agents` | | **OpenAI Codex CLI** | `~/.agents/skills/` | `--agents` | | **Hermes Agent** | `~/.hermes/skills/` | `--hermes` | | **Google AntiGravity** | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | `--antigravity` | `--all` (`-All`) detects installed harnesses and copies skills to each harness's path (`~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.hermes/skills`, `~/.gemini/config/skills`); `--burp-mcp` (`-BurpMcp`) wires the Burp MCP server into each. The full *knowledge* layer ports to all five — the slash commands and `/hunt` engine stay Claude-Code-only by design. → [Multi-harness guide](docs/multi-harness.md) --- ## Star History Chart is self-hosted — regenerate with `python3 scripts/gen_star_history.py` (needs `gh auth login`). Refreshes automatically each day via `.github/workflows/star-history.yml`. --- ## Scope — what this bundle is for, and what it isn't This bundle covers the **external attack surface** — anything reachable from the internet without first compromising an internal endpoint. ### In scope - **Bug bounty hunting** — web apps, APIs, SaaS, GraphQL, OAuth, JWT, file upload, IDOR, SSRF, RCE chains - **Web application pentesting** — full hunt-* coverage of OWASP-mapped bug classes + discipline rules - **External red-team engagements** — initial-access against internet-facing enterprise estate: M365 / Entra ID, Okta-as-IdP, SharePoint on-prem (ToolShell + legacy SOAP), VMware vCenter / Workspace ONE, SSL VPN appliances (Cisco / Fortinet / Citrix / Palo Alto / Pulse / SonicWall / F5), Android APK red-team, supply-chain recon - **Cloud misconfig + post-credential escalation** — public S3, IMDS chains, STS AssumeRole, cross-account confused-deputy - **Recon + OSINT** — subdomain enum, identity-fabric mapping, certificate transparency, JS analysis, secret scanning - **Reporting** — H1, Bugcrowd (VRT-aware), Intigriti, Immunefi, plus client-facing red-team deliverable format ### Out of scope (deliberate — not gaps, design decisions) - **Internal Active Directory attacks** — BloodHound, Kerberoasting, ASREProast, DCSync, Pass-the-Hash, AD CS abuse, ntlmrelayx, Responder, PetitPotam, etc. Different operational risk profile; needs different tooling and judgment. **Future bundle, not this one.** - **C2 frameworks** — Cobalt Strike, Sliver, Mythic, Havoc, BRC4 tradecraft. Out of scope for external-only engagement model. - **Post-exploit / persistence / lateral** — Mimikatz/comsvcs LSASS dumping, golden/silver tickets, named-pipe impersonation, persistence (registry, scheduled tasks, WMI events, COM hijacking), token theft. These start after the perimeter has already broken — different bundle territory. - **Evasion** — AMSI bypass, ETW patching, AV/EDR bypass. Tied to C2 tradecraft above. - **iOS pentesting / hardware / RF / ICS** — out of scope by design. - **Binary exploitation / kernel pwn / browser internals** — different skill universe. If you're running an internal red team that includes domain-takeover chains via Kerberos or lateral movement, **this bundle won't help you in those phases** — and we'd rather say that up front than have you find out mid-engagement. The external surface handoff to internal-RT tooling (Impacket, NetExec, CrackMapExec, Rubeus, Certify, BloodHound) is intentionally outside our scope. **Coverage for internal AD and post-exploit may come in a future update.** --- ## What's inside **84 skills**, auto-loaded by topic — no invocation by name. Coverage across the external attack surface: | Category | # | Examples | |---|---|---| | Hunt — web app vuln classes | 58 | XSS, SQLi, SSRF, IDOR, LFI, SSTI, XXE, CSRF, CORS, open-redirect, SharePoint, ASP.NET/NTLM | | Enterprise platform attack ★ | 10 | M365/Entra, Okta, cloud-IAM-deep, vCenter, enterprise VPN, APK/iOS red-team pipelines, supply-chain recon | | Reporting & validation | 7 | triage-validation, evidence-hygiene, report-writing, bugcrowd-reporting | | Recon & OSINT | 5 | web2-recon, offensive-osint, osint-methodology, recon-scope-triage | | Methodology & mindset | 4 | bb-methodology, bug-bounty, redteam-mindset, bb-local-toolkit | Full searchable catalog → **[docs/skills.md](docs/skills.md)**. Also ships **15 slash commands** (`/hunt`, `/recon`, `/report`, …) and a deterministic **engagement engine** (`engine/`) that maps a target's attack surface and routes each finding to the skill that handles it. --- ## How it works A 6-phase, non-linear workflow — **recon → map & rank → hunt → validate → report** — with scope enforced in code and a **7-Question Gate** before anything is submitted. Two ways to drive it: - **Plain English** — describe what you're testing and the relevant skill loads automatically. - **`/hunt` scaffold + `cbh` CLI** — engagement-folder structure, state, and orchestration. → [Usage guide & worked example](USAGE.md) · [6-phase architecture & skill-to-phase map](docs/architecture.md) · [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md) --- ## Authorization These skills are intended for assets you **own** or have **written authorization to assess** (bug-bounty in-scope assets, pentest engagement letters, CTF challenges, your own infrastructure). The skills include validation gates that auto-trigger when you point Claude at unverified third-party targets — `triage-validation`'s 7-Question Gate explicitly asks whether the asset is in scope (Q3) and on the program's accepted-impact list (Q2). The `bugcrowd-reporting` skill includes researcher-side hygiene (Bugcrowdninja alias, account-state restoration, friendly-tester posture) that signals legitimate authorized testing to the target's fraud team. The bundle explicitly **excludes**: weaponizing 0-days against unauthorized targets, post-exploitation tooling, malware development, mass-targeting infrastructure. See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) for the full posture. > **Heads-up — Anthropic runtime cyber safeguards.** Anthropic's models apply real-time safeguards that **block "vulnerability exploitation or offensive security tooling development" by default** — so even *authorized, in-scope* work can hit a refusal that isn't this bundle's doing. If you do authorized offensive security (pentest / bug bounty / red team), enroll in Anthropic's **free, application-based [Cyber Verification Program (CVP)](https://claude.com/form/cyber-use-case)** to get safeguards adjusted for legitimate dual-use work. (Mass data exfiltration and ransomware development stay prohibited and are *not* adjustable.) Details: [Anthropic — real-time cyber safeguards](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604842-real-time-cyber-safeguards-on-claude). ### Why your model switched mid-session Separate from refusals, and easy to miss. On **Opus 5**, a narrow set of higher-risk cyber requests — Anthropic names *exploit generation*, *binary-based vulnerability scanning* and *penetration testing* — **fall back to Opus 4.8** rather than being refused. You get a notice and the response is labelled with the model that answered, but in a long agentic run that is easy to scroll past, so it can look like Opus 5 quietly got worse. See [why Claude switched models](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16049681-why-claude-switched-models-in-your-conversation-with-opus-5). What to do depends on what you are actually doing: | Situation | What helps | |---|---| | **Auditing your own code** — reviewing a repo you own for defects | Say so. "Defensive review of my own repo", "check this against the OWASP Top 10", "secure refactor to remediate" describe the work accurately and read as remediation. This is not a workaround; the work genuinely is defensive. | | **Authorized offensive work** — live engagement, PoC for a bounty submission | This is what the bundle is for, and the supported route is [CVP](https://claude.com/form/cyber-use-case). Do not reword an offensive engagement to look defensive to get past a classifier — enroll instead. | | **You just want the switching off** | Settings → Capabilities disables automatic model switching. | `/hunt` states the engagement frame (authorized, scope-bounded, remediable finding) on its first turn for exactly this reason — engagement context belongs in the session explicitly, not implied. --- ## Documentation | Doc | Contents | |---|---| | [`README.md`](README.md) | This file — overview, quickstart, scope, skill summary | | [`INSTALL.md`](INSTALL.md) | Full setup with Burp MCP integration and optional skill regenerator | | [`USAGE.md`](USAGE.md) | Workflow walkthrough · decision tree · worked engagement example | | [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) | 6-phase architecture · skill-to-phase mapping · engagement composition | | [`docs/cbh-cli.md`](docs/cbh-cli.md) | `cbh` CLI — native runner orchestrating recon + classify + triage + report | | [`docs/cve-coverage.md`](docs/cve-coverage.md) | CISA KEV coverage snapshot — refreshed weekly via the workflow template at `docs/automation/cve-refresh.yml.template` | | [`docs/credits.md`](docs/credits.md) | Full attribution: 43 original skills + 8 vendored from upstream | | [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) | PR guidelines · skill quality standards · scope | | [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) | Authorized-use posture · responsible disclosure · what's excluded | | [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) | MIT | | [`NOTICE`](NOTICE) | Upstream-skills attribution · no-redistribution note | | [`LICENSE-CONTENT`](LICENSE-CONTENT) | CC BY 4.0 (skill methodology, wordlists, docs) | --- ## Why this exists Most bug-hunting Claude setups are either too generic (one big "security" prompt) or too fragmented (you bookmark 30 disclosed reports and re-read them every engagement). Neither scales past the second target. This bundle was built and validated through authorized engagements that exposed different capability gaps: **Bug-bounty engagement** — surfaced four gaps a starter 3-skill stack could not close: 1. **No hypothesis discipline** — drafts written before validation → wasted hours, hurt validity ratio 2. **No per-program reporting tactics** — VRT defaults auto-downgraded P3-worthy findings to P4 3. **No engagement coordination** — findings, evidence, and submission IDs scattered across folders 4. **No evidence hygiene** — screenshots leaked cookies and victim PII **External red-team engagement** — exposed five additional gaps that bug-bounty defaults made worse: 1. **Conservative defaults retracted real findings** — WAPT mindset stopped tests early on defended targets where red-team continuation would have surfaced bypass chains → `redteam-mindset` 2. **No mid-engagement situational awareness** — client SOC patched confirmed SQLi within 30 min; external attacker locked 14 accounts during a live test session — both invisible without explicit detection methodology → `mid-engagement-ir-detection` 3. **No enterprise-platform attack chains** — M365 + Entra ID, on-prem SharePoint, Cisco SSL VPN, vCenter, and 7 Android APKs all needed current 2024-2026 CVE knowledge and platform-specific tradecraft → `m365-entra-attack`, `okta-attack`, `hunt-sharepoint`, `hunt-aspnet`, `hunt-ntlm-info`, `vmware-vcenter-attack`, `enterprise-vpn-attack`, `apk-redteam-pipeline` 4. **No client-facing deliverable format** — bug-bounty report templates don't fit enterprise red-team where output is a 50KB+ MD + DOCX with embedded screenshots → `redteam-report-template` 5. **No post-credential escalation model** — when recon yielded credentials (AWS keys, JWTs, GCP JSON), it was unclear what they granted or how to escalate → `cloud-iam-deep` The per-class `hunt-*` skills address gap-zero (*"what should I look for in webapps"*) — the original 24 codifying patterns from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports, with 20+ framework/surface skills added by the community v3 expansion — Claude knows the actual chain templates real triagers paid for, not abstract OWASP Top 10. The enterprise-platform and red-team-tradecraft layers address what bug-bounty alone cannot: external red-team engagements against monitored enterprise targets. --- ## Roadmap - [x] HackerOne MCP integration — [`mcp/hackerone/`](mcp/hackerone/README.md): disclosed-report duplicate search, program stats and scope; optional logged-in mode for private programs and your own reports - [ ] Per-engagement memory layer — pattern recall across targets - [x] Industry-specific hunt skills — `hunt-fintech-graphql` shipped; `hunt-healthcare-fhir`, `hunt-gov-compliance` still open - [x] Program-scope importer — `cbh scope import` builds `scope.md` from a program's published scope (HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Intigriti, YesWeHack via [bounty-targets-data](https://github.com/arkadiyt/bounty-targets-data); HackerOne MCP output for private programs; or pasted program text), failing closed on anything ambiguous — see [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md) - [ ] Refresh `hunt-*` skills with newer disclosed reports (re-run `public-skills-builder`) - [ ] Additional enterprise-platform skills — `citrix-netscaler-deep`, `f5-bigip-attack`, `ad-cs-attack` (AD Certificate Services) - [ ] Refresh enterprise-VPN CVE matrix quarterly to track 2026 advisories - [ ] Update architecture SVG to include the 7-skill enterprise-platform layer --- ## Sponsors

**[ApiSmart](https://www.apismart.ai/)** unifies leading LLM, image, and video models through one OpenAI-compatible API. Use one key to switch models, simplify billing, and improve reliability with automatic failover.

**[ThreatWatch360](https://threatwatch360.com)** is an AI-powered offensive-security platform: continuous Attack Surface Management, AI-assisted penetration testing, brand protection, dark-web monitoring, and Cyber Threat Intelligence in one platform. Validated findings with proof-of-concept and business-impact prioritization — signal over alert fatigue. --- ## About Operational tradecraft accumulated across bug-bounty engagements and authorized pentests, codified into Claude skills. Platform-agnostic — slot into any engagement workflow you already use, or none. **Author:** [ElementalSoul](https://github.com/elementalsouls) · GenAI Security Research **Sister project:** [Claude-OSINT](https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-OSINT) — paired skills for the recon phase that this bundle picks up after. Its two recon skills (`offensive-osint`, `osint-methodology`) are **canonically maintained here** and re-exported there, so the two are byte-identical. **Installing both is safe:** each bundle's installer (`install.sh` on macOS/Linux, `install.ps1` on Windows) records a manifest, the script skips re-copying an identical skill, and `--uninstall` keeps any skill the other bundle still owns — uninstalling one never breaks the other. **Vendored foundation:** [shuvonsec/claude-bug-bounty](https://github.com/shuvonsec/claude-bug-bounty) — methodology, validation, reporting, payload library (8 of 84 skills + 15 slash commands) **Generator tool used (not vendored):** [shuvonsec/public-skills-builder](https://github.com/shuvonsec/public-skills-builder) — used to scaffold per-class skills from H1 disclosed reports **Inspirations:** - [archangel / douglasday](https://hackerone.com/) — top-10 H1 hunter; per-class skill pattern - [Trail of Bits — `trailofbits/skills`](https://github.com/trailofbits/skills) — skill-authoring discipline - [SecSkills — `trilwu/secskills`](https://github.com/trilwu/secskills) — subagent pattern **Tool inventory:** - [PortSwigger Burp Suite + MCP Server extension](https://portswigger.net/burp) - [ProjectDiscovery](https://github.com/projectdiscovery) — subfinder · dnsx · httpx · katana · nuclei - [SecLists](https://github.com/danielmiessler/SecLists) · [Assetnote Wordlists](https://wordlists.assetnote.io/) ## License This project is dual-licensed: - **Code** (Python helpers, shell scripts) — [MIT](LICENSE). - **Content** (skill methodology, wordlists, regex catalogs, severity rubrics, docs) — [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International](LICENSE-CONTENT) (CC BY 4.0). It encodes proven patterns and methodologies refined through automated generation processes. The playbook distills key insights from successfully building all 18 diverse, production-ready harnesses. ### Critical Lessons | Lesson | Description | |--------|-------------| | **Use the real software** | The CLI MUST call the actual application for rendering. No Pillow replacements for GIMP, no custom renderers for Blender. Generate valid project files → invoke the real backend. | | **The Rendering Gap** | GUI apps apply effects at render time. If your CLI manipulates project files but uses a naive export tool, effects get silently dropped. Solution: native renderer → filter translation → render script. | | **Filter Translation** | When mapping effects between formats (MLT → ffmpeg), watch for duplicate filter merging, interleaved stream ordering, parameter space differences, and unmappable effects. | | **Timecode Precision** | Non-integer frame rates (29.97fps) cause cumulative rounding. Use `round()` not `int()`, integer arithmetic for display, and ±1 frame tolerance in tests. | | **Output Verification** | Never trust that export worked because it exited 0. Verify: magic bytes, ZIP/OOXML structure, pixel analysis, audio RMS levels, duration checks. | > See the full methodology: [`cli-anything-plugin/HARNESS.md`](cli-anything-plugin/HARNESS.md) --- ## 📦 Installation & Usage ### For CLI-Hub Users ```bash # Install the package manager pip install cli-anything-hub # Browse, search, inspect, and install CLIs cli-hub list cli-hub search cli-hub info cli-hub install # Manage installed CLIs cli-hub update cli-hub uninstall cli-hub launch [args...] ``` ### For Plugin Users (Claude Code) ```bash # Add marketplace & install (recommended) /plugin marketplace add HKUDS/CLI-Anything /plugin install cli-anything # Build a CLI for any software with a codebase /cli-anything ``` ### For Generated CLIs ```bash # Install any generated CLI cd /agent-harness pip install -e . # Verify which cli-anything- # Use cli-anything- --help cli-anything- # enters REPL cli-anything- --json # JSON output for agents ``` ### Running Tests ```bash # Run tests for a specific CLI cd /agent-harness python3 -m pytest cli_anything//tests/ -v # Force-installed mode (recommended for validation) CLI_ANYTHING_FORCE_INSTALLED=1 python3 -m pytest cli_anything//tests/ -v -s ``` --- ## 🤝 Contributing We welcome contributions! CLI-Anything is designed to be extensible: - **New software targets** — Use the plugin to generate a CLI for any software with a codebase, then submit your harness via [`cli-anything-plugin/PUBLISHING.md`](cli-anything-plugin/PUBLISHING.md). - **Methodology improvements** — PRs to `HARNESS.md` that encode new lessons learned - **Plugin enhancements** — New commands, phase improvements, better validation - **Test coverage** — More E2E scenarios, edge cases, workflow tests ### Limitations - **Requires strong foundation models** — CLI-Anything relies on frontier-class models (e.g., Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.4) for reliable harness generation. Weaker or smaller models may produce incomplete or incorrect CLIs that require significant manual correction. - **Relies on available source code** — The 7-phase pipeline analyzes and generates from source code. When the target software only provides compiled binaries that require decompilation, harness quality and coverage will degrade substantially. - **May require iterative refinement** — A single `/cli-anything` run may not fully cover all capabilities. Running `/refine` one or more times is often needed to push the CLI's performance and coverage to production quality. ### Roadmap - [ ] Support for more application categories (CAD, DAW, IDE, EDA, scientific tools) - [ ] Benchmark suite for agent task completion rates - [ ] Community-contributed CLI harnesses for internal/custom software - [ ] Integration with additional agent frameworks beyond Claude Code - [ ] Support packaging APIs for closed-source software and web services into CLIs - [x] Produce SKILL.md alongside the CLI for agent skill discovery and orchestration --- ## 📖 Documentation | Document | Description | |----------|-------------| | [`cli-anything-plugin/HARNESS.md`](cli-anything-plugin/HARNESS.md) | The methodology SOP — single source of truth | | [`cli-anything-plugin/README.md`](cli-anything-plugin/README.md) | Plugin documentation — commands, options, phases | | [`cli-anything-plugin/QUICKSTART.md`](cli-anything-plugin/QUICKSTART.md) | 5-minute getting started guide | | [`cli-anything-plugin/PUBLISHING.md`](cli-anything-plugin/PUBLISHING.md) | Distribution and publishing guide | Each generated harness also includes: - `.md` — Architecture SOP specific to that application - `tests/TEST.md` — Test plan and results documentation --- ## ⭐ Star History If CLI-Anything helps make your software Agent-native, give us a star! ⭐

REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion. Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine. ## Quick start **[Get started at rea.tools](https://rea.tools/get-started/)** for step-by-step instructions by operating system, agent, and analysis provider. ### Connect your agent (MCP) With [Node.js and npm](docs/reference/supported-targets.md) installed, run this from a trusted directory outside the project you plan to analyze. ```bash npx rea-agents setup ``` Choose your agent, review and approve the setup plan, then restart your agent. Setup backs up existing configuration and adds REA's MCP connection and investigation skill. See the [installation guide](docs/getting-started/installation.md) for supported clients, plugins, manual registration, and troubleshooting. Try asking your agent: ```text Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project. ``` Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand. ### Use REA from the terminal (CLI) Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR: ```bash npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json ``` The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence. Replace the path with your target, such as `"D:/apps/example"` on Windows. To install the `rea` command for regular use: ```bash npm install --global rea-agents rea --help ``` For native analysis, configure a provider first. The [CLI and Evidence guide](docs/getting-started/cli.md) covers provider selection, native commands, snapshots, and scripting. For Linux prerequisites, see the [installation guide](docs/getting-started/installation.md#linux-owned-process-prerequisite). ### Update REA For a global npm or Bun installation, run the updater and follow its setup instructions. ```bash rea update ``` If you use `npx`, refresh your agent setup with: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` Review the setup changes and restart your agent. See [update and uninstall instructions](docs/getting-started/installation.md#diagnose-update-and-remove) for package runner options and troubleshooting. ## Showcases

DX-Ball: reconstruct a sound-pan calculation

Recover a position-to-pan helper from x86 instructions and verify the C reconstruction against 3,205 original-x86 cases and all 63 compiled function bytes.

Read the case study · Reconstruction repository

Notion: trace the Electron clipboard bridge

Follow the renderer’s clipboard API through preload and IPC into the main process to see how Notion handles rich clipboard data.

Read the case study

TH04: recover a DOS bullet-ring calculation

Recover fixed and aimed angle calculations from the PC-98 game’s 16-bit instructions and compare the reconstructed C++ with historical compiler output.

Read the case study · Reconstruction repository
If you've used REA on something interesting, we'd love to see it. Share your case in an [issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) or a [pull request](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pulls), including the target, your question, how REA helped, and what you found. ## How REA works Your agent uses REA through MCP to inspect a target and trace the relevant code. It can use the evidence REA returns to ask follow-up questions, explain behavior, or build and test an implementation. The CLI uses the same workflows. ![REA investigation flow: your agent asks about a local target, REA inspects and traces it using analysis tools, and the agent uses the returned code, references and unknowns to explain, implement and test.](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg) [Open the full-size figure](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg). ## What you can analyze REA covers native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, websites, .NET assemblies, Android apps, firmware, and recorded runtime and network activity. [Supported targets and requirements](docs/reference/supported-targets.md) For native decompilation, choose a provider that supports your target format and host OS. See [choosing a deep analysis provider](docs/reference/supported-targets.md#choosing-a-deep-analysis-provider). ## Build RL environments Build a local environment from a recorded web session or a Linux desktop app so an agent can practice a task and check its result. [Build an RL environment with REA](https://rea.tools/guides/rl-environments/). ## FAQ
Which agents can use REA? Any agent that supports local MCP servers. Setup configures the [supported agents](docs/getting-started/installation.md#supported-agents); other clients can use [manual MCP registration](docs/getting-started/installation.md#mcp-registry).
Do I need a native analysis engine? Deep native analysis uses Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna, depending on the target and operation. Static JavaScript and .NET inspection work without a native analysis engine. Setup can install Hopper after approval; Ghidra, IDA and Kuna use your existing installations. See [provider setup](docs/getting-started/installation.md#hopper) for the options and their supported targets.
Do I need to start Hopper first? REA starts Hopper when an operation needs it. On macOS, a first-run dialog may ask you to choose demo mode or activate your license. Complete that prompt in the same user session before your first CLI/MCP operation or unattended job. Open Hopper manually if needed. See [Hopper startup and troubleshooting](docs/getting-started/installation.md#launcher-paths-and-troubleshooting).
What does installing the skill from skills.sh do? The skill supplies investigation instructions for your agent. Use `npx rea-agents setup` to register REA's MCP server and install the matching instructions, then restart your agent. See [skill-only installation](docs/getting-started/installation.md#skill-only-installation).
What code does REA return? Native analysis returns pseudocode and assembly. JavaScript/Electron analysis recovers modules and their relationships. Your agent uses these findings to write and test an implementation; the [showcases](#showcases) give worked examples.
Does REA upload my app? REA analyzes targets locally. Your agent receives the tool results, and its model provider has its own data policy.
What should I do if I hit a bug? Update first; a recent release may already fix it. For a CLI installed with `npm install --global` or `bun add --global`: ```bash rea update ``` For agent setup through `npx`: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` If you're using an agent, complete the [setup refresh](#update-rea) and restart it. Retry the same task. If the problem persists, [open an issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) with your REA version, target type, steps to reproduce and error output.
## Documentation Start with the website's [worked guides](https://rea.tools/guides/). For exact options, prerequisites and result contracts: - [Installation and setup](docs/getting-started/installation.md): agent registration, provider configuration, updates and uninstall. - [Readiness and troubleshooting](docs/getting-started/installation.md#check-readiness-for-your-task): diagnose one agent or analysis engine. - [CLI and Evidence](docs/getting-started/cli.md): commands, provider selection, snapshots, import/export and exit statuses. - [MCP contracts](docs/reference/mcp-contracts.md) and [agent prompts](docs/getting-started/mcp-prompts.md): tool results, sessions and guided investigations. - [Tool catalog](docs/reference/mcp-contracts.md#generated-catalog): generated inventory of tools, providers and CLI commands. Report vulnerabilities through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Community & Support - **Discord** — Ask questions and share what you’re investigating with our passionate community of over 50,000 reverse engineers and builders! [![Join the REA Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Join%20Discord-5865F2?style=flat-square&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/GkcryMnJDM) - **Twitter / X** — Follow [@reatools](https://x.com/reatools) for updates and announcements. - **Feedback & Ideas** — Want a new feature or support for a file format? [Open a GitHub issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) or [join our Discord](https://discord.gg/GkcryMnJDM) and let us know. ## Star history 🎉 **400,000 GitHub stars — thank you!** Thanks to everyone using REA, reporting bugs, requesting features, testing builds, and contributing fixes. ## Contributing We'd love your help with REA! [Open an issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) to report a bug or suggest a feature, or [send a pull request](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pulls) to improve the code or docs. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup and checks. See the [testing guide](docs/development/testing.md) for verification lanes. ## Disclaimer See [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md) for responsible-use guidance. The project's position on illegal or unauthorized use covers all REA versions, distribution channels, and platforms; each copy retains its applicable licenses. REA is for lawful research, education, interoperability, software preservation, and analysis of software you own or are authorized to examine. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) REA-authored code is licensed under MIT. Third-party material retains its own licenses and copyright notices; see [Third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for the dependency inventory, preserved license texts, and external-tool terms. **You must legally obtain and be authorized to use commercial tools**, including IDA Pro / Hex-Rays decompilers, Hopper, and JEB, under their applicable licenses. REA grants no tool license, key, or activation entitlement. Trials and demos remain subject to vendor terms, including user, feature, automation, and output sharing restrictions. Cracked copies, stolen keys, unauthorized key sharing, and bypassing license restrictions are not authorized. This guidance does not amend MIT or third-party licenses.

shirudo is a BPF-based security platform for Linux. After boot-time initialization, it restricts BPF program loads from userspace to signed loaders. Operators ship signed micropatches, called [upatches](https://docs.shirudo.dev/upatches/learn/concepts.html), and verify a target's measured upatch state with TPM-signed evidence. shirudo (Japanese シールド, pronounced “shee-roo-doh”) means “shield”. Read the announcements of shirudo on the blogs of [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/) and [Cisco](https://isovalent.com/blog/post/cisco-openai-shirudo/). ## Quickstart - [Try shirudo in a local VM](https://docs.shirudo.dev/start/quickstart.html). The VM uses a software TPM. - [Read the documentation](https://docs.shirudo.dev/). shirudo is pre-release. Production targets require a Linux kernel with the signed-loader ABI and shirudo's kernel patches, plus a TPM 2.0. See the [system requirements](https://docs.shirudo.dev/operate/plan/system-requirements.html). CI runs all test tiers on x86-64 and host tests on arm64. The test VM also boots locally on arm64. Target validation for riscv64 is pending. The operator and target may use different architectures. See [architecture support](https://docs.shirudo.dev/contribute/arch-support.html). ## Use cases - **Runtime security and observability.** Observe process executions, network activity, and privilege changes with the included [`kernel-obs` package](upatches/kernel-obs/README.md). - **Live mitigations.** Use BPF upatches to block vulnerable paths at kernel hooks or Java upatches to guard application code. - **System hardening.** Use BPF upatches to enforce policies for containers, Kubernetes Pods, and LLM agents. - **Embedded and edge devices.** Deliver signed mitigations to devices with long update cycles. ## Properties - **Boot-time enforcement.** On production targets, enforcement starts when `shirudo init` attaches its guards from the initrd. The guards protect shirudo's runtime and state from root on the target without the operator's signing key. - **Signed and sealed BPF.** BPF upatch loads and unloads go through loaders that the kernel verifies against the sealed `.bpf` keyring. - **Signed Java agents.** shirudo verifies Java upatches in userspace. Configured JVMs load the agents at startup. See [Java agent upatches](https://docs.shirudo.dev/upatches/write/java-agents.html). - **TPM measurement.** Changes to the loaded upatch set extend a per-boot TPM register. `shirudo attest` returns evidence that operators can verify offline. - **Upatches** are small logically contained programs that engineers and agents can read, generate and maintain. Commands take and produce structured data. - **Pull-based delivery.** Targets use one-shot commands to pull packages from OCI registries and export telemetry to configured OpenTelemetry collectors. The [threat model](https://docs.shirudo.dev/security/threat-model.html) states where each of these mechanisms stops. ## How it works [![The operator host builds, signs and pushes to an OCI registry. The target pulls, its kernel checks the signature and runs the loader, its TPM extends the register and signs evidence, which the operator verifies.](Documentation/images/start-how-it-works.svg)](https://docs.shirudo.dev/start/how-it-works.html) BPF upatch lifecycle, from signing through offline verification. [Follow the numbered steps](https://docs.shirudo.dev/start/how-it-works.html). ## By role - New to shirudo: [FAQ](https://docs.shirudo.dev/start/faq.html) - Operators, who deploy and run targets: [Deployment checklist](https://docs.shirudo.dev/operate/deploy/deployment-checklist.html), then [Read shirudo status](https://docs.shirudo.dev/operate/run/read-status.html) - upatch authors: [Your first upatch](https://docs.shirudo.dev/start/guides/first-upatch.html), then [From a kernel fix to a upatch](https://docs.shirudo.dev/upatches/learn/kernel-fix-tutorial.html) - Security reviewers: [Security model](https://docs.shirudo.dev/security/security-model.html), then [Threat model](https://docs.shirudo.dev/security/threat-model.html) - Contributors: [Develop locally](https://docs.shirudo.dev/contribute/code/develop-locally.html) ## Specifications - [Beefile](https://docs.shirudo.dev/reference/formats/beefile.html): the Beefile that describes a package - [.upatch format](https://docs.shirudo.dev/reference/formats/upatch-format.html): the little-endian container with an architecture-neutral signature - [upatch tree](https://docs.shirudo.dev/reference/formats/upatch-tree.html): the operations, segments and publication document of a upatch tree - [Keepalive](https://docs.shirudo.dev/reference/formats/keepalive.html): the record a target sends its collector, its [body](https://docs.shirudo.dev/reference/formats/keepalive.html#keepalive-body-format) and its TPM quote ## Releases [main](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/commits/main/) is the development branch. Development packages are available as run artifacts from the [Build packages](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/actions/workflows/packages.yml) workflow. Release tags publish their packages on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/releases). For upgrades of shirudo and the kernel on a target, consult [Upgrade shirudo and the kernel](https://docs.shirudo.dev/operate/maintain/upgrade.html). ### Software Bill of Materials Every package comes with a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) in [SPDX](https://spdx.dev/) format. ## Project status [![Build packages](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/actions/workflows/packages.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/actions/workflows/packages.yml) [![CI suite](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/actions/workflows/tests.yml) [![Sanitizers](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/actions/workflows/sanitizers.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/actions/workflows/sanitizers.yml) [![Proofs](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/actions/workflows/proofs.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/actions/workflows/proofs.yml) [![CodeQL](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/actions/workflows/codeql.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/actions/workflows/codeql.yml) [![Documentation](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/actions/workflows/docs.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/actions/workflows/docs.yml)
[![Coverage Status](https://coveralls.io/repos/github/shirudo-dev/shirudo/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://coveralls.io/github/shirudo-dev/shirudo?branch=main) [![Coverity Scan Build Status](https://scan.coverity.com/projects/33401/badge.svg)](https://scan.coverity.com/projects/shirudo-dev-shirudo) [![OpenSSF Best Practices](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/17035/badge)](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/17035) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.scorecard.dev/projects/github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo/badge)](https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo) ## License shirudo is licensed under the [BSD-2-Clause License](LICENSE). BPF programs are dual-licensed BSD/GPL. Each source file holds an SPDX license identifier. The tree vendors a few source files from third-party projects under different but compatible licenses; those files retain their original SPDX identifier and copyright notices.

A lightweight, cross-platform remote desktop for computers, browsers, mobile devices, and terminals, with DeskHub for viewing and controlling multiple desktops.

Website · Download · Build guide · Open Web Client · 中文

[![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20iOS%20%7C%20Android%20%7C%20HarmonyOS-blue?style=flat)](#download) [![Clients](https://img.shields.io/badge/client-Desktop%20%7C%20Mobile%20%7C%20Web%20%7C%20CLI-2ea44f?style=flat)](#download) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/kunkundi/crossdesk?style=flat)](https://github.com/kunkundi/crossdesk/releases) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40chunkdash%2Fcrossdesk-cli?style=flat)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chunkdash/crossdesk-cli) [![Build](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/kunkundi/crossdesk/build.yml?style=flat&label=build)](https://github.com/kunkundi/crossdesk/actions/workflows/build.yml) [![License: GPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--3.0-blue?style=flat)](LICENSE) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/kunkundi/crossdesk?style=flat&label=stars)](https://github.com/kunkundi/crossdesk/stargazers)

## Special Sponsors

HuaLongAI 华龙算力

A stable, efficient API relay for Codex, zero-injection Kiro, and Claude models. HuaLongAI sources 100% of its models directly from official providers, with no substitutions. It offers high availability and reports an average SLA above 99.2%. Token-level billing lets you verify each charge. Enterprise contracts and invoices are available.
## Overview CrossDesk connects your computers from desktop, browser, mobile, and terminal clients, with a desktop wall for viewing and controlling multiple devices together. It is built on [MiniRTC](https://github.com/kunkundi/minirtc) and supports self-hosting. [Features](#features) · [Download and platforms](#download) · [Build guide](#build) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Terminal CLI](#cli) · [Agent / MCP](#mcp) · [Direct IP](#lan-direct) · [Trusted devices](#trusted-devices) · [Preview](#preview) · [User guide](docs/USER_GUIDE_EN.md) · [Self-hosting](#self-hosting) · [Documentation and feedback](#development) · [Sponsor](#sponsor) ## Features - **Cross-platform access:** control Windows, macOS, and Linux desktops from computers, browsers, or native iOS / Android clients. HarmonyOS PC and mobile clients are in development. - **Direct IP over LAN:** connect to a desktop from Android, iOS, HarmonyOS, or another desktop using an IP address, port, and six-character password without a cloud signaling service. You can change the port, remember passwords, and view recent devices separately by mode. - **Terminal controller:** view and control remote desktops by device ID, with ANSI / Kitty / Sixel rendering, zoom and pan, persistent local command mode, a Pi extension, and a build independent of the desktop GUI. - **DeskHub:** live multi-device previews, groups, enlarged control, group input, and batch file distribution. - **Video and audio:** H.264 and AV1 video, hardware codecs, remote audio, and in-session quality, frame-rate, and remote display resolution controls. Native sessions can use H.265 when both peers support hardware HEVC encoding and decoding through Media Foundation or NVIDIA codecs on Windows, VideoToolbox on macOS, or NVIDIA codecs on Linux. Confirmed resolution choices are remembered; the original display mode is restored when the last controller disconnects. Capabilities depend on the platform and device. - **Everyday controls:** monitor switching, keyboard and mouse input, shortcuts, and text clipboard. A dual-pane file browser supports directory navigation, bidirectional file and folder transfers, drag and drop, and transfer management. - **Agent / MCP:** authorize an Agent through a local MCP service to observe and operate remote computers, with live monitoring, manual takeover, multiple sessions, clipboard, and file tools. Install the package for your local platform. - **Trusted devices:** optionally restrict desktop access to trusted device identities in addition to the connection password. Copy and paste pairing information to approve devices before they connect. - **Deployment:** direct P2P connections, TURN relay, SRTP media encryption, self-hosting, Windows access before sign-in, and Linux headless operation. ## Download and platform support Get a package matching your OS and CPU architecture from the [website](https://www.crossdesk.cn/) or [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/kunkundi/crossdesk/releases), or open the [Web Client](https://web.crossdesk.cn/) directly. | Platform | Support and installation | | --- | --- | | Windows | **Control + host**. Windows 10+, x64; `.exe` installer, with portable builds also supported | | macOS | **Control + host**. macOS 14.0+; x64 / arm64 `.pkg` for Intel / Apple Silicon | | Linux | **Control + host**. Ubuntu 20.04+, glibc 2.31 baseline; amd64 / arm64 `.deb` | | iOS / iPadOS | **Control only**. Install from the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6828859211); check the listing for its OS requirements. Current source targets iOS 16.0+ and can also be built and signed locally | | Android | **Control only**. Android 8.0+, arm64; install the signed APK or build from source | | HarmonyOS PC (development) | **Control + host**. API 26, arm64; build and sign a HAP with DevEco; physical-device validation is ongoing | | HarmonyOS phones / tablets (development) | **Control only**. API 20+, arm64; build and sign a HAP with DevEco; physical-device validation is ongoing | | Web | **Control only**. A WebRTC-capable browser; no client installation on the controlling device | | Terminal CLI (development) | **Control only**. Distribution targets: macOS / Linux (x64, arm64) and Windows (x64). [Install from npm](#cli-npm) or build from source; see the [CLI guide](apps/cli/README.md) (Chinese) for system requirements and compatibility | | MCP (development) | **Control only**. Operate and watch a remote computer in Codex or DSH. DSH needs one plugin package; Codex also needs Node.js 22+. See [installation and usage](apps/mcp/README.md) (Chinese) | Choose the package for your operating system and processor. Some development features may not be available in released packages; check the release notes for your download. - **Linux:** use `crossdesk-linux-…deb` for an existing desktop, or `crossdesk-virtual-desktop-xfce-…deb` for a server needing a separate Xfce desktop. Choose one. See [installation details](docs/USER_GUIDE_EN.md#installation) and [headless operation](docs/HEADLESS_EN.md). - **macOS:** grant Screen Recording and Accessibility when prompted on first launch. These enable desktop capture and remote keyboard/mouse input. See [permissions](docs/USER_GUIDE_EN.md#installation). - **iOS:** install from the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6828859211). Unsigned GitHub artifacts still require signing; see the [iOS build guide](apps/ios/README.md). HarmonyOS requires a signed DevEco build; see the [HarmonyOS guide](apps/harmony/README.md) (Chinese). ## Build guide The desktop client uses Xmake. Install Git, Xmake 3.1.1 or newer, and the toolchain and dependencies for your platform, then clone the source and submodules: ```bash git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/kunkundi/crossdesk.git cd crossdesk ``` - **Desktop:** follow the [Windows](docs/BUILD_EN.md#windows), [macOS](docs/BUILD_EN.md#macos), or [Linux](docs/BUILD_EN.md#linux) steps to configure, build, and run. See the [full build guide](docs/BUILD_EN.md) for packaging, signing, and CI configuration. - **Mobile and HarmonyOS:** [iOS / iPadOS](apps/ios/README.md), [Android](apps/android/README.md), [HarmonyOS phones / tablets](apps/harmony/README.md), and [HarmonyOS PC](apps/harmony/desktop-port/README.md) (Chinese). - **Terminal and integrations:** [CLI build and usage](apps/cli/README.md) and [MCP build and integration](apps/mcp/DEVELOPMENT.md) (Chinese). ## Quick start ### Connect by device ID 1. **Prepare the host.** Install and run CrossDesk on the computer to control, select ID mode, and wait for the server-connected status, then find its ID and password under **Local Desktop**. 2. **Connect.** On another computer, enter the host's 9-digit ID and click **Connect**. Native mobile clients and the [Web Client](https://web.crossdesk.cn/) can also connect. 3. **Verify the password.** Enter the host's current connection password and wait for the desktop to appear. On desktop, select **Remember password** to reconnect later from **Recent Connections**. For self-hosting, connect both ends to the same service and update the server before upgrading clients. See the [user guide](docs/USER_GUIDE_EN.md#quick-start) for connection steps and the [FAQ](docs/FAQ.md#english) for connection, video, and input problems. ### Connect directly over LAN On a phone or tablet, paste the address shown by the host into **Device ID or IP address** on the home screen and enter the host’s **Direct IP password**. For a desktop controller, follow these steps. 1. **Switch modes.** Open the desktop client on both computers. Click the top-left mode button to select **Direct IP mode**. If the button is hidden, select **Enable direct IP** under **Settings → General → Network** and save. 2. **Enter the address.** On the controller, enter the host's displayed `IP:port`, for example `192.168.1.20:52888` or `[2001:db8::20]:52888`, and click **Connect**. Omitting the port uses **52888**; use the actual port shown on the host. 3. **Enter the password.** Use the host's **six-character ASCII letter/digit password** shown in Direct IP mode. You can select **Remember password**. Switching modes also switches the recent device list. The controller and host must be mutually reachable over a LAN or VPN. Internet access may be available or absent; direct sessions do not depend on a cloud signaling service. The main window lets you select the local IP, edit its port, and change the password. **Listen on all IP interfaces** is enabled by default for IPv4, IPv6, VPN, and other local interfaces on a shared port; change it under **Settings → General → Network**. Disabling **Enable direct IP** stops listeners, disconnects direct IP sessions, and hides the mode button. See the [direct IP guide](docs/USER_GUIDE_EN.md#lan-direct). ### Allow only trusted devices (optional) The desktop trusted-device restriction is **off by default** and applies to both ID and direct IP connections. When enabled, the controller must pass the existing password verification and prove possession of a pairing private key recognized by the host. Knowing the ID and password alone does not satisfy this restriction. 1. **Copy pairing information on the controller.** Open **Settings → General → Privacy → Manage trusted devices**. Under **This device’s pairing info**, click **Copy pairing info**. 2. **Add the controller on the host.** Open the same management dialog, paste the information into **Add a trusted device**, and click **Add**. It is saved immediately, with no second confirmation or prior remote connection required. 3. **Enable the restriction on the host.** Return to settings, select **Only allow trusted devices**, and save. Connect by ID or IP and verify the password as usual. Pairing information contains only the public key, device name, and ID, with no private key or password. Exchange it through a trusted channel. After adding a device, use **View fingerprint** to compare it with the controller. You can also add the local device; the same public key is not added twice. Trust is one-way: to control each other, add the other device on both computers. Adding or removing a device takes effect immediately. With the restriction enabled, **Remove trust** disconnects that device’s sessions, and an empty list rejects all controllers. The dialog also lets you add connected controllers that have completed identity verification. **Compatibility:** Use a recent desktop, iOS, Android, or HarmonyOS mobile client with pairing support. On a phone or tablet, copy the pairing information under **Settings → This device’s pairing info** and add it on the host computer. Older clients and the current terminal CLI cannot connect to a host with this restriction enabled. Before reinstalling, clearing application data, or moving to another computer, see [identity backup and migration](docs/CONNECTIONS.md#backup) (Chinese). ## Session controls and settings Remote sessions support monitor switching, video quality and frame-rate controls, audio, text clipboard synchronization, and bidirectional file transfers. The toolbar also provides network statistics and privacy screen controls. Desktop settings configure direct IP availability, trusted-device restrictions, codecs, relay, self-hosting, video pausing when minimized, and the DeskHub video budget. For Windows, macOS, and Linux X11 hosts, **Video settings → Resolution** selects a mode supported by the current remote display without reconnecting. Desktop and native mobile controllers remember confirmed choices and reapply them on reconnection when still supported. When the last controller disconnects, the host restores the display mode used before the first change in that connection period. Linux requires X11 capture and RandR; Wayland / XWayland resolution changes are not currently supported.

The CLI supports monitor selection, quality settings, detail zoom, panning, and optional keyboard/mouse control. It builds independently of the desktop GUI. ANSI character rendering Kitty pixel graphics
Colored characters show the desktop in standard terminals; use +/- or the wheel to zoom at the mouse position. Pixel graphics display the desktop in terminals supporting the Kitty graphics protocol, such as Ghostty.
ANSI displays characters; Kitty displays pixels. Appearance depends on terminal support, font, and window size. ### Install from npm and connect Install **Node.js 22 or later** and npm, then get [@chunkdash/crossdesk-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chunkdash/crossdesk-cli). npm selects the native executable for your OS and CPU architecture; Xmake and a C++ toolchain are not required. ```sh npm install -g @chunkdash/crossdesk-cli@latest crossdesk-cli doctor --json crossdesk-cli 123456789 ``` Replace `123456789` with the host's 9-digit device ID and enter its password at the hidden prompt. Connections start in read-only, silent mode; `doctor` checks the local environment without connecting. To update, run `npm install -g @chunkdash/crossdesk-cli@latest` again. You can also use `npx` without a global installation. The first run downloads the matching platform package: ```sh npx @chunkdash/crossdesk-cli@latest doctor --json npx @chunkdash/crossdesk-cli@latest 123456789 ``` Install the main `@chunkdash/crossdesk-cli` package with npm optional dependencies enabled; do not add `--omit=optional`. Installing a platform package alone does not register the `crossdesk-cli` command. See the [npm distribution guide](apps/cli/docs/npm-distribution.md) (Chinese) for platform requirements, migration from older packages, and troubleshooting. ### Everyday controls Connections start read-only and silent. Press `c` in read-only mode to enable keyboard and mouse input, `+/-` or the wheel to zoom, and `f` to restore the full desktop. **To quit while controlling the host, press `Ctrl+]`, then `q`**; ordinary keys otherwise go to the remote computer. ```sh # Character graphics in a standard terminal crossdesk-cli 123456789 --renderer ansi # Pixel graphics in a terminal supporting the Kitty graphics protocol crossdesk-cli 123456789 --renderer kitty ``` The CLI connects by device ID. Direct IP, audio playback, file transfer, clipboard synchronization, and hosts with trusted-device restrictions are not currently supported. The host needs CrossDesk and an available desktop session. Self-hosted servers must support CLI connections.
